observation.visible_scene: A macro close-up of a single rectangular pat of pale-yellow butter resting on top of a horizontal cob of plump yellow corn kernels, set against a solid black background. The butter occupies the upper-center of the frame, with rows of kernels visible beneath it.
visible_changes: The butter's sharp edges and corners gradually soften and round off throughout the segment, indicating an already ongoing melting process rather than a sudden onset.

The bottom edge of the butter sags and bulges downward into the gaps between the kernels, developing an increasingly wavy, drooping contour that is most pronounced near the center-right in the later frames.
A glossy, wet sheen of melted butter spreads across the kernels directly under and around the pat, becoming more noticeable on the left side toward the end of the clip.
The top face of the butter stays roughly level and in the same vertical position, so the change is deformation/phase change of the pat, not translation of it.
The corn cob and the black background hold fixed positions frame-to-frame, so the apparent changes are object deformation, not camera motion.
outside_clip_unknowns: The heat source or cooking context that is driving the melt is not visible.
Whether the butter was solid when first placed, and the final extent of melting beyond this segment, are unseen.
Any earlier contact or settling that may have preceded the crop boundary is unknown.
uncertain_details: The exact moment the melt first became visually detectable is not pinpointed; softening is subtle at the start.
Minor apparent shifts in the butter's silhouette could partly reflect a very slow camera drift, though background evidence suggests the camera is essentially static.
